title: Street Levels in the Tyropoeon Valley
author: R. W. H[amilton]
location_note: Shafts II and III on the line of the main sewer in Tariq el Wad, south of David Street, Old City of Jerusalem; placed by name.
reading: pp. 105-108 in full; p. 110 in full; p. 109 (drawings) by keyword
notes: Municipal sewer repair 1931: two superimposed streets; the excavator's hypothesis assigns the lower to the Herodian city and the upper to the early Byzantine period (coin of the First Revolt, year 2, from the shaft, not stratified). A comb-picked vault at the bottom of Shaft II, function unknown, is not coded. Signed 'R. W. H.' (p. 110).

features.subtype: lower, mortared part of the main drain, contemporary with the lower pavement
features.period: with the lower street, assigned by hypothesis to the Herodian city
features.quote: the lower and better-built part of the drain is contemporary

features.subtype: sewer in its present form with vault and manholes, contemporary with the upper street
features.period: with the upper street, assigned to the early Byzantine period
features.quote: the sewer in its present form is contemporary with the upper

features.subtype: side water conduits A, B, C and at least two more, flowing east, cut by the sewer
features.period: C earlier than the lower street; B between the two streets; A uncertain
features.quote: to have been water conduits rather than drains
